title: ServerMessage
description: Discriminated union of all server (Pi) -> client (phone) messages. See design doc §7.2.

solverBenchMs.description: Host score on the canned solver benchmark, milliseconds (measured once at server startup). The client times the SAME solve in its wasm solver and compares to decide where the final solve runs (solver placement). Null while the host benchmark has not finished.

MappingStopped.description: Reply to stop_mapping with solveOnHost=false (the client's benchmark chose phone-side solving): the capture is stopped and the session log persisted, but NO host reconstruction runs. The client solves locally (wasm) and uploads the result via submit_map; the counts echo what the server logged, as a sanity check against the client's local buffers.

t0.description: Echoed phone clock at original send, in milliseconds.

t1.description: Server clock at receive of ping, in milliseconds.

t2.description: Server clock at send of pong, in milliseconds.

patternClockEpoch.description: Server-clock time of the start of a known cycle, in milliseconds.

PatternState.description: Reply to get_pattern: whether a capture is running and, if so, the pattern clock it is running against. codeParams is always present (the server default when inactive) so a pattern follower can lay out its display before mapping starts.

patternClockEpoch.description: Server-clock time of the start of a known cycle, in milliseconds; null when no capture is active.

LiveMap.description: Reply to get_live_map: the latest interim reconstruction of the active capture. `map` is null until the continuous solver has produced its first solve (or when no capture is active). Interim maps are in-memory only; the persisted, full-quality map still arrives via result_ready after stop_mapping.

SolveStatus.description: Reply to get_solve_status: the final solve's live state, updated by the optimizer's progress callback. All-null fields when no solve is running (or the running solver does not report progress, e.g. the fast pose-trusting path). `leds` is a LIGHTWEIGHT interim position list for the converging preview (full quality metrics only exist in the final OutputMap); `trajectory` is the decimated solved camera path, same gauge as `leds`.

progress.description: Estimated optimizer progress in [0,1] (evaluation budget consumed); null when unknown.

CountingState.description: Reply to set_counting_pattern: whether a counting pattern is now displayed (active = the commanded blocks were non-empty) and the server-clock time it latched, so the phone knows when its camera view is valid to read.

epochMs.description: Server-clock time the pattern took effect, ms; null when inactive.

LedCountState.description: Reply to set_led_count: echo of the persisted per-channel strip length.

PlaybackState.description: Reply to set_playback / get_playback: the effective playback configuration (the player echoes what it is actually running, with its defaults filled into params).

mapId.description: The stored map/topology playback runs on; null when the player has none selected.

FrameTiming.description: Reply to get_frame_timing: a drained batch of rendered-frame timestamps (the player samples its monotonic clock as it pushes each mapping-pattern frame to the LEDs) plus the number of samples dropped to ring-buffer overflow since the last poll. Even bitPeriodMs spacing between successive tMonoMs means smooth generation; gaps mean the pattern render loop stalled that long. Forwarded by the phone to the trace server for offline stutter analysis.

patternClockEpoch.description: Active capture's pattern-clock epoch (player-clock ms); null when no capture is running (ticks then empty).

bitPeriodMs.description: Expected inter-frame spacing (the mapping bit period).

cycleFrames.description: Frames per pattern cycle, so a tick's cycle is seq / cycleFrames.

dropped.description: Samples lost to ring-buffer overflow since the last poll (the phone did not drain fast enough).

seq.description: Absolute frame index since the pattern epoch, BEFORE the cycle-length modulo.

tMonoMs.description: Player monotonic clock when the firmware pushed this frame to the LEDs. Milliseconds, but sampled from the microsecond clock so it carries sub-millisecond precision for the inter-frame gaps.
